sources.notes: Inert schedule(parameters, closure) definitions, immediate invocation, dynamic convergence, and one-time instances use the shared graph.

Hosted and workflow-only applications lower workflow cron through the shared schedule graph and emit a focused schedule-control worker with exact workflow-gateway authorization and target-specific fixed-schedule resources. Named concrete schedulers such as Hatchet retain their qualifier and run in that worker; only a qualified unresolved target-selected scheduler is excluded as external. The web host runs the deterministic scheduler only during local Vite development and never embeds deployment-target scheduler providers. Generated-worker live Hatchet evidence remains provider qualification rather than source-contract evidence.

Hosted and workflow-only durable future starts lower to a shared one-time occurrence through the focused schedule-control boundary. The local Vite development host uses the deterministic scheduler. Exact live Hatchet occurrence and provider-resource cleanup remain provider qualification evidence.

Function-native dynamic schedules converge through the shared graph, persist canonical desired state before provider projection, and are served by a generated schedule-control worker on deployed targets or the deterministic Vite host during local development. Generated-worker restart/live lifecycle remains provider qualification evidence.
Processor checkpoint, partition, and consumer lifecycle remain processor semantics and are not exposed as public schedule parity.
Alarm authority, actor identity, persisted timer state, and turn ordering remain actor-owned.
Image/command CronJobs are target-specific infrastructure and never claim function-native parity.

providers.remaining: Bounded history policy and fresh generated-product restart/teardown qualification. Canonical persistence and admitted-occurrence recovery are covered deterministically.

Live-qualified on OrbStack for the atomic active-instance ceiling, fail-closed high-cardinality admission, duplicate occurrence fencing, prior receipt recovery, terminal retry receipt, PostgreSQL-authority restart recovery, provider create/no-op/drift repair/UID-preserving update/disable/delete, owned cleanup, generated event-callback create/update/restart-repair/remove, and a real generated Job that reads Kubernetes' authoritative CronJob scheduled-time annotation through least-privilege jobs/get RBAC before completing the generated occurrence endpoint and durable receipt. This row does not claim EventBridge or arbitrary raw Kubernetes image/command CronJobs.

Live-qualified on OrbStack for fixed and dynamic firing, dynamic replacement update, disable and deletion, exact one-time scheduled-at preservation, two provider-deletion/schedule-control-replacement repairs, PostgreSQL occurrence authority, durable-workflow non-regression, and leak-free TypeKro/Alchemy teardown. This row does not claim Kubernetes CronJob, EventBridge, or arbitrary external Hatchet lifecycle behavior.

Deterministic tests prove interrupted provider projection recovery, but real-AWS create/no-op/update/one-time/disable/duplicate/retry/DLQ/drift/interruption/delete and cost evidence remains; all-bounded remains an explicit compatibility rejection.
